Google Ads Conversion Tracking Malaysia (2026) | ADV

← All guides & resources

Google Ads Conversion Tracking · 2026 Guide

## Google Ads Conversion Tracking: Not Converting, or Not Counting?

When a Malaysian business tells us Google Ads is not converting, the ads are often fine. The count is wrong. This guide covers what to track, how each type of lead is tracked, and how to check your own setup in 15 minutes.

Get a Free Account Audit
Run the 15 Minute Check

"Smart Bidding can only chase what you count."

The short answer

If Google Ads looks like it is not converting, check the tracking before you touch the ads. In Google Ads, open Goals, then Conversions, then Summary, and confirm three things: every lead action shows a healthy tracking status, only real enquiries (form submits, WhatsApp clicks, calls, purchases) are set as primary, and lead actions count One conversion per click, not Every. If any of those fail, Smart Bidding is optimising to the wrong number, and no ad rewrite will fix that.

### Is Google Ads not converting, or is it not counting?

Often the ads are fine and the count is wrong. Smart Bidding learns only from the conversions you report, so check the count first.

Not converting

Clicks arrive. Nobody enquires.

Look at Search terms, ads and the landing page, once tracking is clean.

Not counting

People enquire. Google Ads never hears, or hears the wrong things.

Why it hurts more Report zero and Smart Bidding learns nothing. Report too many and it buys the wrong traffic.

Same account, two ways of counting

Read the detail
Two different problems hide behind "Google Ads is not converting". One is real: clicks arrive and nobody enquires. The other is counting: people do enquire, but Google Ads never hears about it, or hears about the wrong things.

The counting problem does more damage. Smart Bidding sets bids from the conversions you report. Report zero and it has nothing to learn from. Report an inflated number and it buys more of the wrong traffic. Our main Google Ads guide calls this the first leak: conversions that are not revenue. This page is the practical version.

So before you rewrite ads or blame the agency, confirm the count. When we take over an account through our Google Ads management service , tracking is checked before a single bid changes.

### What should count as a conversion for a Malaysian SME?

The moment someone raises their hand. For most Malaysian SMEs that is a form, a WhatsApp click, a call or a purchase.

Lead form Count: One

Tracked by The Google Ads tag on a real submit, or an imported GA4 event.

Watch Fire on the submission, not when the form page loads.

WhatsApp

Tracked by A click on your wa.me link or WhatsApp button.

Limit It records the click, not a sent message.

Phone call

Tracked by Number clicks on your mobile site, call ad clicks, or imported call conversions.

Limit Google forwarding numbers are not available in Malaysia, so Google does not measure real call length.

Purchase Count: Every

Tracked by The Google Ads tag on the order confirmation page, with value and transaction ID.

Watch The transaction ID stops a page reload counting one order twice.

WhatsApp is a proxy. Compare WhatsApp clicks with the chats your team actually received each week.

Read the detail
A conversion is the moment someone raises their hand. For most Malaysian SMEs, that means one of four actions.

Action | How it is tracked | What to know

Lead form | Google Ads conversion tag (Google tag or Google Tag Manager) on a real submission, or a GA4 event imported into Google Ads | Fire on the submission, not when the form page loads. Count: One.

WhatsApp | A click event on your wa.me link or WhatsApp button, set up as a website conversion | It records the click, not a sent message. Some people open WhatsApp and never type.

Phone call | Clicks on a number on your mobile website, Clicks on call ads and assets, or Import call conversions | Google forwarding numbers are not available in Malaysia, so Google does not measure real call length here.

Purchase | Google Ads tag on the order confirmation page, with the order value and a transaction ID | Count: Every. The transaction ID stops a page reload counting the same order twice.

WhatsApp is a proxy. Google Ads cannot see inside a chat, only the click on your button. Compare clicks with the chats your team actually received that week. If clicks are double the real chats, your true cost per lead is roughly double what Google Ads reports.

Calls are similar. Google's call reporting runs on Google forwarding numbers, and Malaysia is not on Google's list of countries where they are available (Source: Google Ads Help, About call reporting, checked October 2026) . Google says mobile number clicks track the click, not the call, and for call ad clicks it estimates whether a meaningful call happened. If calls matter, log them in a CRM and use Import call conversions (Source: Google Ads Help, About phone call conversion tracking, 2026) .

### Google Ads tag or GA4 import: which should you use?

Both work. Pick one source per action and make it primary, or every lead gets counted twice.

Option 1

Google Ads tag

What it does Sends the conversion straight to Google Ads.

Trap Do not also make a GA4 import of the same form primary.

Option 2

GA4 import

What it does Shares a key event from Google Analytics with Google Ads.

Trap Secondary by default. Switch it to primary inside Google Ads, or Smart Bidding ignores it.

Read the detail
Both work. The Google Ads tag sends the conversion straight to Google Ads. A GA4 import shares a key event from Google Analytics with Google Ads.

Two traps. Google says conversions created from Google Analytics are secondary by default and can only be updated to primary in Google Ads (Source: Google Ads Help, About primary and secondary conversion actions, 2026) , so a perfect GA4 lead event can still be ignored by Smart Bidding. And if the tag and the import both track the same form as primary, every lead counts twice. Pick one source per action and make it primary.

### What is the difference between primary and secondary conversions?

Primary actions drive bidding. Secondary actions are for watching only. Make primary only the actions you would pay for.

Primary

Conversions column. Used for bidding.

Form submit WhatsApp click Call Purchase

Secondary

All conversions column. Not used for bidding.

Page views Scroll depth Time on site

Where each conversion action goes

Read the detail
Primary actions are reported in the Conversions column and used for bidding when their goal is used for bidding. Secondary actions are observation only: they show in All conversions and are not used for bidding, unless they sit inside a custom goal (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026) .

Google warns that getting this wrong can stop Smart Bidding from optimising effectively. Primary should hold only actions you would pay for: a form submit, a WhatsApp click, a call, a purchase. Page views, scroll depth and time on site belong in secondary, if anywhere.

### Which tracking faults make Google Ads look like it is not converting?

Six faults we look for first on any account. Each one either hides real leads or invents fake ones.

01

#### Duplicate counting

Red flag Leads double on paper. Your inbox does not change.

Why it happens
The same form tracked by the tag and a GA4 import, both primary, or the tag installed twice. Leads double on paper. Your inbox does not change.

02

#### Page views counted as leads

Red flag The account looks brilliant while the phone stays quiet.

Why it happens
A "conversion" that fires when someone loads the contact or pricing page. The account looks brilliant while the phone stays quiet.

03

#### A thank-you page that fires on load

Red flag Reached without submitting, through a menu link, bookmark or search.

Why it happens
People reach it without submitting, through a menu link, a bookmark or search. Google notes that reloading a confirmation page can fire the tag again, and a transaction ID lets it drop duplicate purchases (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026) . For leads, set Count to One and keep the page out of menus and search.

04

#### Count set to Every for leads

Red flag Every repeat submit counts as another lead.

Why it happens
Google recommends One conversion for leads and Every conversion for purchases. But Every is the default for website actions, so many lead forms count every repeat submit (Source: Google Ads Help, About conversion counting options, 2026) .

05

#### Tags not firing

Red flag Unverified, Tag inactive or Needs attention in the Tracking status column.

Why it happens
A site rebuild or new form plugin quietly breaks the tag. Google shows Unverified, Tag inactive or Needs attention in the Tracking status column (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026) . Leads keep arriving, Google Ads sees none, and Smart Bidding has nothing to work with.

06

#### Consent settings that block tags

Red flag A banner that blocks tags until visitors respond can make conversions vanish.

Why it happens
See the next section . It matters less for Malaysian traffic than most articles suggest.

### Do you need enhanced conversions and Consent Mode v2 in Malaysia?

Enhanced conversions is stage two, once you have a CRM. Google's Consent Mode v2 requirement covers EEA traffic, and Malaysia is not in the EEA.

#### Enhanced conversions for leads

What it does Sends hashed form details with each enquiry. Later you import CRM sales and Google matches them to the ad click.

Does it apply in Malaysia? Suits sales that close offline, like a clinic or insurance agent. Needs a working CRM, so treat it as stage two.

#### Consent Mode v2

What it does Passes visitors' cookie choices to Google and adjusts how Google tags behave.

Does it apply in Malaysia? Google's requirement to collect and share consent applies to advertisers receiving data from users in the European Economic Area. Malaysia is not in the EEA, so for Malaysian traffic that requirement is not why conversions are missing. It matters if you get European visitors or already run a consent banner.

Read the detail
Enhanced conversions for leads. Enhanced conversions sends first-party data from your form, such as an email address, hashed with SHA256, to improve the accuracy of conversion measurement (Source: Google Ads Help, About enhanced conversions, 2026) . The leads version is built for sales that close offline. Your form sends hashed details when the enquiry arrives. When that lead becomes a customer, you import the same details from your CRM and Google matches the sale to the ad click (Source: Google Ads Help, About enhanced conversions for leads, 2026) . For a clinic or an insurance agent, this teaches Smart Bidding the difference between an enquiry and a customer. It needs a working CRM and an import through Google Ads Data Manager or the API, so treat it as stage two.

Consent Mode v2. Consent mode passes visitors' cookie choices to Google and adjusts how Google tags behave. Version 2 added two signals, ad_user_data and ad_personalization. Google's requirement to collect and share consent applies to advertisers receiving data from users in the European Economic Area (Source: Google Tag Manager Help, Updates to consent mode for traffic in the EEA, 2026) . Malaysia is not in the EEA, so for Malaysian traffic that requirement is not why conversions are missing.

It matters if you get European visitors or already run a consent banner. Google says basic consent mode blocks tags until the visitor responds to the banner, while advanced mode loads tags with consent denied, sends cookieless pings and supports an advertiser-specific conversion model (Source: Google Ads Help, About consent mode, 2026) . A banner that blocks tags can make conversions vanish. Malaysian privacy law is a question for your lawyer.

### How do you check your conversion tracking in 15 minutes?

Six checks, no developer. You need admin access to Google Ads and your phone.

-
01 3 min

Read the tracking status

Goals, then Conversions, then Summary. Flag Unverified, Tag inactive or Needs attention.

-
02 3 min

List what is primary

For each primary action, ask: would I pay for this? If not, make it secondary.

-
03 2 min

Check the count setting

Leads should be One. Purchases should be Every.

-
04 2 min

Look for duplicates

Two primary actions for the same thing, like a form tag and a GA4 lead event? Keep one.

-
05 3 min

Run a live test

In Tag Assistant, submit a test form and click WhatsApp and call. Each fires once. Nothing fires on page load.

-
06 2 min

Compare against reality

Last week's conversions against real enquiries. Double, either way, means something is broken.

Found a fault? Fix the count first, then leave bidding alone while it settles. It is the first thing we check in a Google Ads audit .

Read the detail

- Read the tracking status (3 minutes). Go to Goals, then Conversions, then Summary. Anything showing Unverified, Tag inactive or Needs attention goes to the top of the list. Hover on the status for a Troubleshoot option that opens Tag Assistant.

- List what is primary (3 minutes). For each primary action, ask: would I pay for this? If not, make it secondary.

- Check the count setting (2 minutes). Leads should be One. Purchases should be Every.

- Look for duplicates (2 minutes). Do two primary actions describe the same thing, such as a form tag and a GA4 lead event? Keep one.

- Run a live test (3 minutes). Open your site in Tag Assistant. Submit the form with a test entry, then click your WhatsApp and call buttons. Each should fire once, and nothing should fire when a page simply loads. Then open the thank-you page directly. If a conversion fires, anyone can trigger it.

- Compare against reality (2 minutes). Compare last week's Google Ads conversions with the enquiries that reached your inbox, WhatsApp and CRM. A small gap is normal. Double, either way, means something is broken.

If you find a fault, fix the count first and leave bidding alone while the account settles, or you cannot tell which change moved the numbers.

### What does bad tracking actually cost?

Bad tracking never appears on your invoice. It appears as decisions made on the wrong number.

RM64 vs RM105

Cost per conversion, newer service line against the main Search campaign. Only fair if both count the same action.

RM91.47

Overall CPA, up from RM55.11 across four consecutive 30 day readings.

~100

Phantom leads a month if a duplicate tag catches one lead in ten, on 1,000 real leads.

~9%

How much better cost per lead then looks than it really is.

First two: a healthcare group we manage, 30 days to 5 Oct 2026, on our Live Results Board . Last two: a worked example.

Read the detail
Take a healthcare group we manage. In the 30 days to 5 October 2026, a newer service line campaign ran at RM64 per conversion against RM105 for the main Search campaign. That comparison guides where the next ringgit goes, and it only holds if both campaigns count the same action the same way. If one counted page views, the "cheaper" campaign could be the worse one.

The account's overall CPA has risen across four consecutive 30 day readings: RM55.11, RM61.45, RM69.46, RM76.78, then RM91.47 (175 conversions on RM16.1K). It is an uncomfortable trend, and it stays on our Live Results Board . A count padded with page views would have hidden it.

Scale raises the stakes. Take an account getting 1,000 real leads a month at RM5 per lead. A duplicate tag on one lead in ten adds about 100 phantom leads a month, and cost per lead looks about 9% better than it really is. Smart Bidding then chases the wrong signal.

Clicks are not cheap either. Top of page bids in Malaysia run from RM4 to RM77 for "google ads conversion tracking" and RM13 to RM320 for "google ads malaysia" (Source: Google Keyword Planner, Malaysia, October 2026) . Bids vary hugely by keyword, but every click bought on bad data is real money. See Google Ads pricing in Malaysia , how Google compares with other channels , and our Performance Max guide , where clean data matters even more. If you want tracking kept clean as part of ongoing work, it sits inside our Google Ads agency service .

Common questions

### Conversion tracking, answered plainly.

The questions Malaysian business owners ask when Google Ads says one thing and the inbox says another.

Why is my Google Ads not converting?
+

Check the tracking before you change the ads. Many accounts that look like they are not converting have a counting problem: a tag that stopped firing after a website change, a lead action set as secondary, or page views counted as leads. In Google Ads, open Goals, then Conversions, then Summary, and read the Tracking status column. If the tracking is clean and enquiries are still low, then look at search terms, ads and the landing page.

Why are my Google Ads conversions not showing?
+

Three common reasons. The tag has not fired yet, which Google shows as Unverified. The tag has stopped firing, shown as Tag inactive. Or the action is secondary, so it appears only in the All conversions column and not in Conversions. Conversions created from Google Analytics are secondary by default and can only be switched to primary inside Google Ads.

Should a WhatsApp click count as a conversion in Google Ads?
+

Yes, if WhatsApp is how your customers enquire, but treat it as a proxy. Google Ads can track the click on your WhatsApp button, not the message. Some people open WhatsApp and never send anything. Each week, compare WhatsApp clicks in Google Ads with the chats your team actually received, and work out your real cost per lead from that.

Should lead conversions be counted as One or Every?
+

One. Google recommends One conversion for leads, because one ad click usually produces one unique lead, and Every conversion for purchases. Every is the default for website conversion actions, so check each lead form action by hand.

Do Malaysian businesses need Consent Mode v2 for Google Ads?
+

Google's consent requirement applies to advertisers who receive data from users in the European Economic Area. Malaysia is not in the EEA, so it is not Google's requirement for Malaysian traffic. It matters if you get European visitors, or if your site already runs a consent banner that blocks Google tags until visitors respond. Malaysian privacy law is a separate question for your lawyer.

Should I use the Google Ads tag or GA4 imported conversions?
+

Both work. The Google Ads tag sends conversions straight to Google Ads. A GA4 import shares a key event from Google Analytics with Google Ads. Pick one as the primary source for each action. If both are primary for the same form, every lead is counted twice.

Google Ads Audit Checklist for Malaysia (2026) | ADV

Google Ads Audit · 2026 Checklist

## The Google Ads Audit Checklist We Use

Eleven checks, in the order we run them on every account that comes to us for a free audit. Do it yourself in an afternoon, or send us view-only access to Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager and Search Console and we will run it for you.

Get a Free Account Audit
Start the Checklist

"If the conversions aren't real, every other number in the account is fiction."

The short answer

A Google Ads audit checks, in order, whether the account counts real leads or sales, whether its money reaches the right searches, and whether its settings let automated bidding learn. Start with conversion tracking, because every other number depends on it, then work through search terms, match types, bidding, budget, ads, landing pages, location settings, Performance Max and account access.

Time needed: about three to four hours for a typical small to mid-size Malaysian account, using the 11 checks below.

How to use this checklist

### How do you audit a Google Ads account?

Work through the 11 checks in order. If check 1 fails, the numbers in checks 2 to 11 are not telling you the truth. Tap "How to check" on any card for the steps.

The audit, ticked in sequence

It is the pre-takeover audit from our guide to fixing Google Ads accounts , laid out so you can run it yourself. Or hand it to our Google Ads management team and we run it free.

Part 1 · The data

### What should you check first in a Google Ads audit?

The data. Smart bidding chases whatever the account calls a conversion, so a broken definition spoils every later finding.

01 30 to 45 min

#### Conversion tracking: is what is counted real?

Red flag Page views or WhatsApp icon clicks counted as primary conversions next to real leads.

How to check

Look at Every conversion action, whether it is Primary or Secondary, and what it fires on. Primary actions fill the Conversions column and drive bidding. Secondary actions are observation only (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Goals menu, then Conversions, then Summary.
Bad looks like Page views or WhatsApp icon clicks counted as primary conversions next to real leads. Two tags firing for one lead. More conversions than the enquiries your team actually received.

If this fails, fix it before anything else. Our Google Ads conversion tracking guide covers the setup.

02 15 min

#### Account structure and campaign types

Red flag Many small campaigns, each too thin to learn.

How to check

Look at Which campaign types are running, how budget splits between them, and whether brand searches sit apart from generic ones.
Where The Campaigns table, last 90 days.
Bad looks like Many small campaigns, each too thin to learn. Brand and generic keywords mixed together, so cheap brand clicks hide an expensive generic campaign.

Part 2 · The waste

### How do you find wasted spend in a Google Ads account?

Read what people really searched, then check that keywords and ads are tight enough to earn good Quality Scores.

03 30 to 60 min

#### Search terms and negative keywords

Red flag Spend on job seekers ("jawatan kosong"), freebie hunters, DIY searches or places you do not serve, in English and in Malay.

How to check

Look at What people actually typed before clicking, over 90 days, sorted by cost. A keyword is what you bid on. A search term is what they searched (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Campaigns, then Insights and reports, then Search terms.
Bad looks like Spend on job seekers ("jawatan kosong"), freebie hunters, DIY searches or places you do not serve, in English and in Malay. A negative keyword list nobody has touched for months.

04 20 min

#### Match types, ad relevance and Quality Score

Red flag Broad match on manual bidding, when Google says it is critical to use Smart Bidding with broad match.

How to check

Look at The mix of broad, phrase and exact match, and Quality Score. Its three components are expected clickthrough rate, ad relevance and landing page experience, each rated Above average, Average or Below average (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Keywords, then the columns icon, then the Quality score section.
Bad looks like Broad match on manual bidding, when Google says it is critical to use Smart Bidding with broad match. Top spending keywords rated Below average on the same component, which shows you what to fix.

Part 3 · The engine

### Are bidding and budget set up so the account can learn?

Automated bidding needs conversions to work with. Budget only helps if you are losing impressions to budget.

05 10 min

#### Bidding strategy versus conversion volume

Red flag A Target CPA campaign with a handful of conversions a month, or targets edited every few days.

How to check

Look at Each campaign's bid strategy, set against the conversions it actually records each month.
Where Each campaign's settings, under Bidding.
Bad looks like A Target CPA campaign with a handful of conversions a month, or targets edited every few days. Google recommends judging Target CPA over the last 30 days with at least 30 conversions (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).

06 10 min

#### Budget and impression share

Red flag Your best campaign losing impressions to budget while a weak one has money to spare.

How to check

Look at Why your ads did not show. Search lost IS (budget) and Search lost IS (rank) split the reason, and both are campaign level columns (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Add both as columns in the Campaigns table.
Bad looks like Your best campaign losing impressions to budget while a weak one has money to spare. Heavy loss to rank, which means Quality Score or bids, so a bigger budget will not fix it.

For realistic RM budgets, see our Google Ads pricing guide and what ads cost in Malaysia .

Part 4 · The offer

### Do the ads and landing pages earn the click?

Both shape the ad quality Google uses in the auction, so both affect what you pay per click.

07 20 min

#### Ads and assets

Red flag One ad per ad group with three headlines.

How to check

Look at Your responsive search ads and the assets around them. Each ad takes up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions, and Ad strength is rated from Poor to Excellent (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where The Ads view and the Assets view.
Bad looks like One ad per ad group with three headlines. Promotions that ended months ago. An old number in a call asset. No mention of WhatsApp, when that is how most Malaysian customers want to reach you.

08 15 min

#### Landing page and speed

Red flag Every ad pointing at the homepage.

How to check

Look at Where each ad sends people, whether the page answers the search, and how it loads on a phone.
Where Campaigns, then Insights and reports, then Landing pages. Check the Mobile-friendly click rate column.
Bad looks like Every ad pointing at the homepage. Slow loading on mobile data. Eight-field forms. Google calls landing page speed one of the easiest ways to improve mobile ad results (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).

Part 5 · The settings

### Which settings quietly leak budget in Malaysia?

Three quick checks that most accounts we review have skipped.

09 5 min

#### Location targeting: Presence or Presence or interest

Red flag A Petaling Jaya clinic left on the default, reaching people outside its area who only searched about it.

How to check

Look at "Presence or interest" is the default and reaches people in, regularly in, or who have shown interest in your targeted locations. "Presence" reaches people in or regularly in them (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Each campaign's settings, under Locations.
Bad looks like A Petaling Jaya clinic left on the default, reaching people outside its area who only searched about it. With Singapore next door and many Malaysians searching from abroad, that traffic is real. Local service businesses usually want Presence. Travel, property and education businesses selling overseas may want the default.

10 20 to 30 min

#### Performance Max checks

Red flag Most conversions coming from your own brand name, with no brand exclusions set.

How to check

Look at Which searches Performance Max is matching, and whether it is taking your own brand searches.
Where Campaigns, then Search terms, then "Search terms and landing pages for Performance Max". Negative keywords in Performance Max only apply to Search and Shopping inventory (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Bad looks like Most conversions coming from your own brand name, with no brand exclusions set. Asset groups with one image and generic text. Nobody checking overlap with Search.

More in our Performance Max guide .

11 10 to 15 min

#### Change history, access and ownership

Red flag Performance swings after changes or auto-applied recommendations nobody approved.

How to check

Look at What changed recently, who can get into the account, and whose account it really is.
Where Campaigns menu, then Change history, which covers the past 2 years. Admin menu, then Access and security.
Bad looks like Performance swings after changes or auto-applied recommendations nobody approved. A former agency or staff member still holding Admin. Only one admin, which Google itself flags as a risk. An account under someone else's login.

After the audit

Common questions

### Google Ads audit questions, answered.

Straight answers on time, order, location settings and what an audit can and cannot do.

How long does a Google Ads audit take?
+

About three to four hours for a typical small to mid-size Malaysian account. The search terms review takes the longest. Accounts with many campaigns take longer.

What should I check first in a Google Ads audit?
+

Conversion tracking. Smart bidding optimises toward whatever the account counts as a conversion, so if page views or button clicks count as leads, every other number is misleading. Fix the data before touching bids, budgets or keywords.

Should I use Presence or Presence or interest in Malaysia?
+

If you only serve customers physically in your area, Presence is usually safer. The default, Presence or interest, also reaches people elsewhere who have shown interest in your location, which can suit travel, property and education businesses selling overseas.

Is the ADV Google Ads audit really free?
+

Yes. Send us view-only access to Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager and Search Console. View-only means we can see campaigns, tags and reports without changing anything. You keep the findings whether or not you hire us. No obligation and no pitch deck.

Can an audit alone lower my cost per lead?
+

No. An audit tells you what to fix and in what order. Savings come from making the fixes and managing the account every week. Our insurance and fintech account took 12 months of sustained work to bring cost per lead from RM4.40 to RM2.41.

# SEO vs AEO vs GEO in Malaysia — Guide
URL: https://advmarketing.biz/seo-aeo-geo-malaysia
==============================================================================

SEO vs AEO vs GEO Malaysia — Get Found & Cited by AI | ADV

← All guides & resources

SEO · AEO · GEO · 2026 Guide

## Found on Google. Cited by AI.

Your customers now ask ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews before they ever see a list of links. This is how SEO, AEO and GEO fit together, why AI skips most Malaysian websites, and the four layers we build so a business gets ranked and named — with the numbers from doing it.

Get a Free AI Visibility Check
Read the Guide

"Ranking gets you listed. Being cited gets you chosen."

The short answer

SEO gets your page ranked in Google's links. AEO gets your answer lifted into the reply — featured snippets and AI Overviews. GEO gets your brand named inside ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. They are layers of one job, not three separate services.

AI engines retrieve from search indexes. ChatGPT search uses third-party providers including Bing, plus OpenAI's own crawler. A page that cannot rank is rarely cited. What decides who gets picked is whether the content is crawlable, answers the question directly, comes from a business the engine can recognise, and contains something specific enough to cite.

Realistic timeline: technical fixes in days, Google positions over 4–8 weeks, AI citations measured monthly against a fixed question set.

Why AI skips most sites

### Ranking is not the same as being named.

The same business, the same 20 questions a buyer would ask — and a different answer from every engine. Four gaps explain most of the difference.

#### 1. AI crawlers are blocked

Often by accident — an old robots.txt rule, or a hosting default. Cloudflare offers an AI-crawler block during setup; we found it switched on while moving our own site in September 2026.

#### 2. The answer is buried

Answer engines lift a paragraph, not a page. If the direct answer sits under three paragraphs of brand story, a competitor's clearer sentence gets used instead.

#### 3. The business isn't an entity

No Organization schema, a different name on Google Business Profile, directories and socials. If an AI can't be sure who you are, it names someone it is sure about.

#### 4. Nothing worth citing

"Award-winning, results-driven" gives an AI nothing to quote. Specific, dated, sourced numbers do — it's why our statistics page reached page 1 before any of our service pages.

What we build

### Four layers. Crawlable first.

The four layers, in order

Layer 1: Make it crawlable. Allow search engines and AI search crawlers in robots.txt, make sure pages render without JavaScript, and submit the sitemap to both Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. Blocking OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot or PerplexityBot can remove you from those tools' search answers. GPTBot and ClaudeBot only control AI training. ChatGPT search uses third-party providers including Bing, plus OpenAI's own crawler, so Bing is not optional. An llms.txt file is an optional extra, not a requirement.

Layer 2: Make it answerable. Put a direct two-to-three-sentence answer at the top of every page and use question-shaped headings. Every guide on this site opens with a "short answer" box for exactly this reason. Structured data helps engines read the page, but Google says no special schema or llms.txt is needed for AI Overviews. Google has retired HowTo rich results, and FAQ rich results now only show for government and health sites. Where we add FAQ or HowTo schema, it matches the visible text word for word.

Layer 3: Make it recognisable. Build one entity graph — Organization and Person schema linked with sameAs to LinkedIn, Google Business Profile and directories — and keep the business name, address and phone identical everywhere.

Layer 4: Make it citable. Publish original, dated, sourced data — statistics pages, published results, expert quotes in the press — then measure a fixed question set every month. Our Malaysia statistics page and Live Results Board are both built to be quoted.

What this has produced

5 weeks

To move our own site from an average Google position of ~60 to ~12, Aug → Sep 2026

Page 1

For our statistics research page — 154 impressions in one week at position 6

13 / 20

Buying-intent questions where Perplexity names our healthcare client

20 / 20

Of those questions now show a Google AI Overview above the links

Common questions

### What Malaysian businesses ask about AI search.

The questions we hear most from owners who've noticed customers asking ChatGPT instead of Google.

What is the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?
+

SEO gets your page ranked in Google's list of links. AEO (answer engine optimisation) gets your answer lifted straight into the reply — featured snippets, Google AI Overviews and voice answers. GEO (generative engine optimisation) gets your brand named and cited inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Mode. They are layers of the same job, not alternatives.

Do I still need SEO if customers ask ChatGPT instead of Google?
+

Yes. AI answer engines retrieve from search indexes. Google AI Overviews draw on Google's index. ChatGPT search uses third-party providers including Bing, plus OpenAI's own crawler. A page that cannot rank is rarely cited. SEO is the entry ticket; AEO and GEO decide whether you are the source that gets picked.

Should I block AI crawlers from my website?
+

Not if you want to be recommended. Blocking OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot or PerplexityBot can remove you from those tools' search answers. GPTBot and ClaudeBot only control AI training. Check your robots.txt and your hosting or CDN settings — Cloudflare offers an AI-crawler block toggle during setup that is easy to leave on by accident.

How long does AEO and GEO take in Malaysia?
+

Technical fixes such as crawler access, schema and answer blocks take days. Google positions typically move over 4 to 8 weeks; our own site went from an average position of about 60 to about 12 in five weeks. AI citations shift more unevenly, which is why we re-test a fixed question set every month.

How do you measure AI visibility?
+

A fixed set of 20 buying-intent questions is run through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google every month, recording whether the brand is named and in what position. Alongside that, AI referral traffic (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai) is tracked as its own channel in Google Analytics.

Can I do AEO and GEO myself?
+

The first two layers, yes: open your site to crawlers, and put a clear two-to-three-sentence answer at the top of every important page. Building a recognisable entity and earning citations from original data and press takes longer and benefits from someone doing it every week.

Get started

### Does AI recommend you, or a competitor?

Send us your website and five questions your customers ask. We'll run them through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google and show you who gets named — you or someone else. Free, and the findings are yours either way.

Message us on WhatsApp

We typically respond within 2 business hours.

What We Deliver

### Six disciplines. One cohesive system.

Most SEO agencies pick one lane. We run technical SEO, content, links, local, and the two new disciplines — AEO and GEO — as a single, coordinated strategy.

#### Technical SEO

Site speed, Core Web Vitals, crawlability, schema markup, XML sitemaps, canonical tags. We fix the foundation so every other piece of SEO work compounds on solid ground.

#### On-Page SEO

Keyword mapping, title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, content optimisation. Every page built to match search intent — not just keyword density.

#### Link Building

High-DR backlinks through PR placements, industry citations, and content-led outreach. No link farms, no PBNs — only links that build real authority.

#### Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO)

Direct answer blocks, question-shaped headings, and structured data so your answer is lifted into featured snippets, Google AI Overviews and voice answers.

#### Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)

Brand entity building, E-E-A-T signals, and original data worth citing, so ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Mode name your brand when buyers ask the questions you need to own.

#### Local SEO

Google Business Profile optimisation, local citations, and Malaysia-specific keyword targeting for Kuala Lumpur and beyond. Built for businesses that need to be found in a specific place.

The shift

### Most SEO agencies are still optimising for 2019.

Traditional SEO — ranking in Google's blue links for clicks — is still important. We do it well. But the way buyers discover answers is changing faster than most agencies are prepared to admit.

ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews are now first touchpoints for millions of searches. When someone asks "who is the best digital marketing agency in KL?" they're increasingly asking an AI — not typing into a search bar.

AEO and GEO are the layers ADV adds on top of standard SEO: content structured so AI tools can extract it, a brand that reads as a recognised entity, and inclusion in generative summaries — not just a ranking.

We run the same schema, entity, and structured-content work on our own site that we build for clients — we don't recommend what we don't do ourselves.

Common questions

### SEO questions, answered honestly.

If your question isn't covered here, message us on WhatsApp — we reply fast and we'll give you a straight answer.

How long does SEO take to show results in Malaysia?
+

Most technical fixes ship within days; results take longer. For rankings, expect 3–6 months for competitive terms in Malaysia — faster for long-tail keywords and local queries. Local SEO for Kuala Lumpur-based terms can show movement within 4–8 weeks when Google Business Profile and citation signals are properly set up.

What's AEO and why does it matter now?
+

AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation) gets your answer lifted straight into the reply: featured snippets, Google AI Overviews and voice answers. As more searches get answered before anyone clicks a link, being that answer is becoming as important as ranking on Google. ADV implements AEO through direct answer blocks, question-shaped headings, and structured data. The SEO vs AEO vs GEO guide walks through how it works.

What's GEO?
+

GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) gets your brand named and cited inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Mode. GEO involves brand entity building, E-E-A-T signals, and original data worth citing, so generative AI includes your business in its answers. It builds on SEO and AEO, and remains a newer, fast-moving discipline even among agencies that have started offering it.

Do you do link building?
+

Yes. ADV builds links through content-led outreach and PR placements — including press mentions and industry citations. Our own Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics page is an example of the linkable research assets we build. We do not use link farms, private blog networks (PBNs), or low-quality directory spam. Every link is earned from a real publication or relevant industry site, and built to withstand algorithm updates.

Can you help with local SEO for KL businesses?
+

Yes. Local SEO is core to our Malaysia service offering. We handle Google Business Profile optimisation, local keyword targeting for Kuala Lumpur and surrounding areas, local citation building across relevant Malaysian directories, and review strategy. Local SEO is particularly effective for service businesses, clinics, retailers, and professional services operating in KL and Selangor.

We've done SEO before with no results — why would this be different?
+

Most SEO engagements fail because they are either technical-only (fixing crawl errors without creating demand) or content-only (publishing blog posts without fixing foundational issues). ADV starts with an audit to identify exactly what went wrong, fixes the technical and structural foundation, then layers AEO and GEO on top — the combination most SEO-only engagements skip. We run this same approach on our own site; we don't recommend what we don't do ourselves.

RM0.59 per landing-page view on a brand-new pixel; mid-flight pivot cut CPL 42–52%
Completed

Methodology: figures come directly from Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads reporting exports — not self-reported estimates. Rows are anonymised by industry vertical because Malaysia is a small market and precise details can identify a business. Completed campaigns keep their final figures on the board.

Why we publish this

### Every agency claims results. Claims are free.

Agency marketing runs on adjectives — "ROI-driven", "performance-focused", "data-led". None of it is checkable. So we made ours checkable: this board carries the actual numbers from actual client accounts, refreshed weekly, including the periods where performance dipped.

The board is also how we work internally. The same automated reporting stack that assembles our weekly client reports — data pull, AI-drafted narrative, human review — keeps this page current. If you hire us, this is the reporting discipline your account gets.

Want the full story behind any row — strategy, creative, budget decisions? See our pricing & results page , or ask us directly.

About the board

### How this works.

The short version of what's behind these numbers.

How often is the board updated?
+

Weekly. Active accounts show their most recent reported period; completed campaigns stay listed with their final figures and are marked as completed.

Why anonymise clients by industry instead of naming them?
+

Client confidentiality. Malaysia is a small market — even without a name, precise details can identify a business. Aggregating by vertical lets us publish real numbers without exposing any individual client.

Where do the numbers come from?
+

Directly from ad-platform reporting — Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads exports — not self-reported estimates. When performance dips, the number still gets published. That's the point of the board.

# Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics 2026
URL: https://advmarketing.biz/malaysia-digital-marketing-statistics-2026

72 Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics 2026 (Updated Oct)

Malaysia Digital Marketing — 2026 Research Report

## Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics You Need to Know in 2026

By Alvin Yap

Founder, ADV Digital Marketing

Last updated: October 6, 2026

Contents

- Key Statistics

- Market Size & Ad Spend

- Social Media Usage

- Paid Advertising

- E-commerce

- SME Digital Adoption

- Consumer Behavior

- AI & Marketing Tech

- Malaysia vs SEA

- Projections 2026–2031

- FAQ

- Sources

Malaysia's digital economy is on a breakout run. With 98% internet penetration, 30.7 million social media user identities, and a digital economy projected at US$39 billion GMV in 2025, the fastest growth rate in Southeast Asia, Malaysia is no longer an emerging digital market. It is the market. This page compiles 72 verified statistics from DataReportal, the e-Conomy SEA report (Google/Temasek/Bain), DOSM, MDEC, and more. Every stat is sourced and dated.

### Key Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics (2026)

The headline numbers across all categories — the stats most frequently cited by journalists, analysts, and marketing teams.

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV was projected to reach US$39 billion (RM161 billion) in 2025, up 19% year on year and the fastest growth rate in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain & Company — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Malaysia's internet penetration reached 98% (35.4 million users) by October 2025 — among the highest rates in Southeast Asia and globally.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysia had 30.7 million active social media user identities in October 2025 (85.0% of the population), up 5.6 million (+22.2%) in a year. DataReportal advises caution when comparing this with earlier editions.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Digital advertising accounted for about 77% of total Malaysian advertising spend in 2024.
(Source: MAGNA, reported by Bernama, 2026)

-
TikTok reports an ad reach of 30.7 million in Malaysia, equal to 86.8% of internet users. DataReportal notes this exceeds the adult population, so it is ad reach, not a count of unique users.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysia's e-commerce GMV was projected at US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY); platform e-commerce grew 47.6% — among the highest growth rates in Southeast Asia.
(Source: e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Momentum Works, 2025)

-
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools daily; 68% have had conversations with AI chatbots; 92% are willing to share data access with AI systems.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
58% of Malaysian consumers have bought a product endorsed by an influencer; 79% of social media users follow at least one influencer.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

### Market Size & Digital Ad Spend

How large Malaysia's digital economy and advertising market are today, and what's driving the growth.

Digital took about 77% of all Malaysian ad spend in 2024, led by social media (41%) and search (24%). MAGNA forecasts digital's share will reach 85% by 2029.
(Source: MAGNA, reported by Bernama, 2026)

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV was estimated at US$31 billion in 2024 (+16% YoY) and projected at US$39 billion in 2025 (+19% YoY), making Malaysia the fastest-growing digital economy in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2024 & 2025, 2024–2025)

-
Malaysia's digital adex reached RM343 million in Q1 2025 (+6.4% YoY) and RM661 million in Q2 2025 (+22% YoY), based on data from 21 media agencies covering approximately 60% of total digital ad spend.
(Source: Media Specialists Association / MAA / MDA, 2025)

-
Social media took 41% of total Malaysian adex in 2024 and search engines 24%, the two largest channels. MAGNA forecast total adex to grow 6.4% in 2025.
(Source: MAGNA, reported by Bernama, 2026)

-
Malaysia's ICT sector contributed RM451.3 billion (23.4% of GDP) in 2024, growing 5.1% year-on-year; ICT GVA alone accounted for 13.9% of GDP.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), 2024)

-
Malaysia approved RM87.4 billion in digital investments in 2025, expected to create more than 31,000 jobs.
(Source: Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), reported by Bernama, 2026)

-
MDEC had targeted a 25.5% digital economy share of GDP by end-2025, up from 23.4% in 2024.
(Source: Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), 2025)

Malaysia Digital Ad Spend — H1 2024 vs H1 2025 (RM million)
Source: MSA / MAA / MDA, 2025. Based on 21 agencies covering ~60% of total market. Q1 2024 and Q2 2024 are back-calculated from reported YoY growth rates (+6.4% and +22% respectively).

Year | Digital Economy GMV (USD) | YoY Growth | Status

2024 | US$31B | +16% | Estimate (e-Conomy SEA 2024)

2025 | US$39B | +19% ★ Fastest in SEA | Projection (e-Conomy SEA 2025)

2030 | US$45B to US$70B | n/a | Projection (e-Conomy SEA 2023)

(Sources: Google, Temasek, Bain: e-Conomy SEA 2023, 2024 and 2025)

### Social Media & Platform Usage

Platform reach, time spent, and growth trends across Malaysia's social media landscape.

Malaysia had 30.7 million active social media user identities (85.0% of population) in October 2025, up 5.6 million (+22.2%) in a year. Malaysians use an average of 8.12 social platforms each month, second in Southeast Asia only to the Philippines.
(Sources: DataReportal Digital 2026: Malaysia; DataReportal Digital 2025)

-
Malaysia had 34.9 million internet users (97.7% penetration) in January 2025, growing to 35.4 million (98.0%) by October 2025 — one of the highest internet penetration rates in the world.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 & 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
TikTok reports an ad reach of 30.7 million in Malaysia in late 2025, equal to 86.8% of internet users and 114.8% of adults aged 18 and above. DataReportal publishes the figure as reported but notes it exceeds the adult population, so treat it as ad reach, not unique users.
(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Platform-reported ad reach in late 2025: YouTube 23.6 million (65.4% of population); Facebook 23.0 million (63.7%); Instagram 16.1 million (44.6%). LinkedIn had 10.0 million registered members (27.7%).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend an average of 2 hours 46 minutes per day on social media and use an average of 8.12 social platforms each month, above the Digital 2025 global average of 6.83 and second in SEA only to the Philippines (8.36).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend an average of 8 hours 13 minutes per day online, ranking second in Southeast Asia to the Philippines (8 hours 52 minutes).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia had 44.0 million active cellular mobile connections in late 2025, equal to 122% of the total population. In early 2025, 99% of connections were broadband (3G, 4G or 5G).
(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026 and Digital 2025: Malaysia, 2025)

Social Media Platform Ad Reach in Malaysia, Late 2025 (millions)
Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026: Malaysia (late 2025). Figures are platform-reported ad reach, not unique users; LinkedIn shows registered members. TikTok's figure exceeds the adult population.

Platform | Ad reach (late 2025) | % of Internet Users

TikTok | 30.7M | 86.8%

YouTube | 23.6M | 66.7%

Facebook | 23.0M | 65.0%

Instagram | 16.1M | 45.5%

LinkedIn (members) | 10.0M | 28.3%

(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025. Ad reach is platform-reported and is not a count of unique users. TikTok's figure exceeds the adult population.)

### Paid Advertising Benchmarks

Ad spend allocation, platform cost benchmarks, and format trends for Malaysian paid media.

Social media's share of Malaysia's digital adex surged to nearly 50% in Q2 2025 — up from 44% in Q2 2024. Programmatic advertising is forecast to represent 73% of all digital ad spend by 2028.
— MSA / MAA / MDA / Digital in Asia, 2025

-
Social media's share of Malaysia's digital adex grew from 41% to 44% in Q1 2025, and from 44% to nearly 50% in Q2 2025 year-on-year.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by Marketing Interactive, 2025)

-
Video advertising accounted for 22–24% of Malaysia's digital ad spend in H1 2025; display accounted for 12–15%; Tech & Electronics was the largest sector at 20% of digital adex.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by BusinessToday, 2025)

-
Travel & Tours surged from 1% of Malaysia's digital adex in Q1 2024 to 9% in Q1 2025 — the fastest-growing advertising category in the country.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by Marketing Interactive, 2025)

-
Meta Ads (Facebook/Instagram) CPM for Malaysia is projected at about US$4.80 and CPC at about US$0.55 in 2026, a projection by Adamigo based on industry benchmarks and late 2025 data.
(Source: Adamigo, Meta Ads CPM/CPC Benchmarks by Country 2026, a 2026 projection)

-
Programmatic advertising is projected to account for 73% of Malaysia's digital ad spending by 2028, driven by AI-powered targeting and automation.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
Meta lead-generation campaigns for a Malaysian EV-charger installer delivered lead conversations at RM13.14 each in the 30 days to 5 October 2026: 844 conversations on RM11,089 of spend, with the best campaign at RM11.55 per lead and a 3.3% CTR.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts, Live Results Board, October 2026)

-
An EV-charger client's Meta awareness campaign ran at RM1.30 CPM (cost per 1,000 impressions) in the 30 days to 5 October 2026, optimised for reach rather than conversions. That is far below Adamigo's 2026 projection of US$4.80 for Malaysian Meta CPMs.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts, Live Results Board, October 2026)

-
A Malaysian healthcare group's Google Ads cost RM91.47 per conversion over the 30 days to 5 October 2026 (175 conversions on RM16.1K of spend), after four rises in a row from RM55.11. A newer service-line campaign converted at RM64, against RM105 for the main Search campaign.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts, Live Results Board, October 2026)

-
Meta lead costs for a Malaysian aesthetics clinic ranged from a best of RM14.04 to RM41.41 per lead conversation in its last reported period in 2026 — a ~3× spread between best and latest periods in the same account, which is why single-month agency case-study figures should be read with caution.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts — Live Results Board, September 2026)

### E-commerce & Mobile Commerce

Platform GMV, consumer shopping habits, and the mobile-first e-commerce reality in Malaysia.

Malaysia's e-commerce GMV reached US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY). Platform e-commerce grew 47.6% — one of the highest growth rates in all of Southeast Asia. Smartphones account for 72.67% of all e-commerce transactions.
— e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Momentum Works / Mordor Intelligence

-
Malaysia's total e-commerce income (including B2B, B2C, and B2G) reached RM1.29 trillion in 2024, up 8.8% from RM1.18 trillion in 2023; B2C alone grew 11.3% to RM374.7 billion.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) — Usage of ICT and E-commerce, 2024)

-
Malaysia's retail e-commerce market was valued at US$10.62 billion in 2025; smartphones account for 72.67% of all e-commerce transactions; digital wallets represent 34.92% of transaction value.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
Shopee is the preferred platform for 65% of Malaysian online shoppers; TikTok Shop is preferred by 26%; Lazada by 11%.
(Source: Vase.ai, Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, survey of 417 consumers, September 2025)

-
88% of Malaysian online shoppers buy via marketplaces; 71% buy via social platforms; only 26% buy directly from brand websites.
(Source: Vase.ai, Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, survey of 417 consumers, September 2025)

-
E-commerce shoppers in Malaysia increased by 16% in 2025, with nearly two-thirds of Malaysians now purchasing online.
(Source: Ipsos Malaysia — E-commerce Landscape in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Live-stream commerce generates up to 22% of some e-commerce platform GMV in Malaysia, reflecting the rise of video commerce; in SEA overall, content/live-stream commerce reached US$49.7 billion (32% of platform GMV) in 2025.
(Source: Digital in Asia / Momentum Works, 2025)

-
Fashion/apparel leads Malaysian e-commerce product categories with 26.67% revenue share; B2C accounts for 80.89% of the market.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
725,285 Malaysian MSMEs had adopted e-commerce platforms by 2025 under the MyDIGITAL blueprint.
(Source: MDEC / MyDIGITAL — Digital in Asia, 2025)

### SME Digital Adoption

How Malaysian small and medium businesses are adopting digital tools — and where the gaps remain.

97.2% of Malaysian businesses used computers and 95.3% used the internet in 2024. Yet in March 2025 the Digital Minister said more than 60% of businesses, over 650,000 MSMEs, were still at a basic level of digitalisation. Near-universal connectivity has not yet translated into advanced digital capability.
(Sources: DOSM, 2024; Ministry of Digital, reported by The Sun, 2025)

-
97.2% of Malaysian businesses used computers and 95.3% used the internet in 2024 (up from 96.6% and 94% in 2023); web presence grew to 74.4% of all businesses.
(Source: DOSM — Usage of ICT and E-commerce, 2024)

-
In an SME Corp Malaysia and Huawei survey of 2,033 SMEs (fieldwork May to June 2018), 44% used cloud computing, mostly for storage only, and 54% used some form of data analytics, mostly spreadsheets.
(Source: SME Corp Malaysia and Huawei, Accelerating Malaysian Digital SMEs white paper, 2018)

-
Malaysian MSMEs contributed RM689.8 billion, or 39.7% of GDP, in 2025, growing 5.7%. They employed 48.7% of Malaysia's workforce.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), MSMEs Performance 2025, July 2026)

-
Malaysia's digital transformation market was valued at US$10.68 billion in 2025; SMEs are the fastest-growing segment, expanding at 19.56% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia Digital Transformation Market, 2025)

-
Malaysia's Budget 2025, tabled in October 2024, allocated RM50 million to a Digital Matching Grant via Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) to accelerate MSME digital transformation.
(Source: Malaysia Ministry of Finance, Budget 2025, 2024)

-
MDEC launched a RM1.5 billion Business Digitalisation Initiative in March 2025, when more than 60% of Malaysian businesses, over 650,000 MSMEs, were still at a basic level of digitalisation.
(Source: Ministry of Digital and MDEC, reported by The Sun, 2025)

### Malaysian Consumer Digital Behavior

How Malaysian consumers research, discover, and buy — and what influences their decisions.

35% of Malaysian consumers purchase a product after seeing it on social media. 58% have bought something endorsed by an influencer, and 79% of social media users follow at least one influencer.
(Sources: Vase.ai survey of 417 consumers, September 2025; INSG.co, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend an average of 8 hours per day on the internet in 2025, placing them among the heaviest internet users in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Ipsos Digital — reported by New Straits Times, 2025)

-
35% of Malaysian consumers purchase a product after seeing it on social media; 49% prioritize discounts when shopping online; 42% compare prices before purchasing.
(Source: Vase.ai, Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, survey of 417 consumers, September 2025)

-
40% of Malaysian consumers practice omnichannel shopping (equal online/offline balance); 39% are primarily online-focused; only 4% shop exclusively in physical stores.
(Source: Vase.ai, Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, survey of 417 consumers, September 2025)

-
71% of Malaysian consumers prefer to shop for fashion online; 84% prefer to buy groceries from physical stores; 60% prefer health & beauty products online.
(Source: Vase.ai, Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, survey of 417 consumers, September 2025)

-
58% of Malaysian consumers have purchased a product endorsed by an influencer; 79% of social media users follow at least one influencer.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
75% of Malaysian consumers turn to influencer tutorial videos to solve problems or learn about products; 34% factor influencer recommendations into their purchase decisions.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Micro-influencers make up 52% of all influencers in Malaysia; nano creators lead on engagement at an average 4.79% engagement rate.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
DuitNow QR transactions reached approximately 3 billion, double the prior year; e-payment transactions totalled 18.4 billion (+25%), averaging 538 per person annually.
(Source: Bank Negara Malaysia / Digital in Asia, 2025)

### AI & Marketing Technology Adoption

How AI is reshaping marketing infrastructure, consumer behaviour, and business investment in Malaysia.

Malaysia attracted US$759 million in private AI investment — representing 32% of all Southeast Asian AI funding — between H2 2024 and H1 2025, making it the dominant AI investment destination in the region. Data centre capacity expanded 5.75× in a single year.
— e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News

-
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools and features daily; 68% have had conversations with AI chatbots; 92% are willing to share data access with AI systems.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Revenue for apps with marketed AI features grew 103% in H1 2025 vs H1 2024 in Malaysia — double the growth rate seen in most other Southeast Asian markets.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Major hyperscaler AI and cloud commitments to Malaysia: Microsoft US$2.2B, Google US$2B, NVIDIA-YTL US$2.36B, Oracle US$6.5B — over US$15 billion collectively.
(Source: MDEC / Digital in Asia, 2024)

-
Malaysia's data centre capacity expanded from 120 megawatts in 2024 to 690 megawatts in H1 2025 — a 5.75× increase in one year — representing 50% of all planned Southeast Asian data centre capacity.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News, 2025)

-
Approximately 73% of Malaysian businesses currently using AI remain at basic automation levels, despite the country's significant infrastructure investment.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia's 5G network covered about 82.4% of populated areas by December 2024. 5G subscriptions grew from 4.6 million in November 2023 to 28.7 million in November 2025.
(Sources: GlobalData, reported by RCR Wireless, 2025; MCMC, reported by Malay Mail, 16 December 2025)

### Malaysia vs Southeast Asia

How Malaysia stacks up against its neighbours across key digital adoption and engagement metrics.

Malaysia grew its digital economy 19% in 2025 — faster than Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, and Singapore — a result analysts described as a "dramatic reversal of regional dynamics."
— e-Conomy SEA 2025, Google/Temasek/Bain

-
Malaysia's internet penetration was 98.0% in late 2025, level with Singapore (98.4%) and just behind Brunei (99.0%). Thailand was at 94.7%, Vietnam 84.2%, the Philippines 83.8% and Indonesia 80.5%.
(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026 country reports, October 2025 data)

-
Social media user identities equalled 85.0% of Malaysia's population in October 2025, second among the six countries compared here. Singapore led at 90.6%, followed by the Philippines (81.9%), Thailand (79.1%), Vietnam (77.6%) and Indonesia (62.9%).
(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026 country reports, October 2025 data)

-
Malaysians use an average of 8.12 social platforms each month, second in SEA after the Philippines (8.36), ahead of Indonesia (7.93) and Singapore (7.24); all SEA nations exceed the Digital 2025 global average of 6.83.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend 8 hours 13 minutes online daily — second in SEA to the Philippines (8 hours 52 minutes) and well above Singapore (6 hours 33 minutes).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia's platform e-commerce grew 47.6% YoY in 2025; SEA overall grew 22.8%; Malaysia's growth rate was among the highest in the region alongside Thailand (51.8%).
(Source: Momentum Works — SEA Platform E-Commerce 2025 Report, 2025)

-
Malaysia's median mobile internet speed reached 143.56 Mbps in August 2025 (+34.2% YoY); fixed broadband reached 154.03 Mbps (+17.6% YoY).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, citing Ookla Speedtest, 2025)

-
Malaysia attracted 32% of Southeast Asia's total private AI funding — the highest national share in the region — between H2 2024 and H1 2025.
(Source: e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News, 2025)

Country | Internet Penetration | Social Media User Identities (% pop.)

Singapore | 98.4% | 90.6%

Malaysia | 98.0% | 85.0%

Thailand | 94.7% | 79.1%

Vietnam | 84.2% | 77.6%

Philippines | 83.8% | 81.9%

Indonesia | 80.5% | 62.9%

(Source: DataReportal, Digital 2026 country reports, all rows October 2025 data. Brunei, not shown, had 99.0% internet penetration.)

### Future Projections: 2026–2031

Where analyst consensus and government targets see Malaysia's digital economy heading over the next five years.

Digital transformation could unlock up to RM257.2 billion (US$61.3 billion) in annual economic value in Malaysia by 2030, according to a 2021 AlphaBeta study.
(Source: AlphaBeta, reported by The Vibes, October 2021)

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV is projected to reach US$45 billion to US$70 billion by 2030, up from a projected US$39 billion in 2025.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain, e-Conomy SEA 2023 and 2025)

-
Malaysia's digital transformation market is projected to grow from US$10.68 billion (2025) to US$29.74 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 18.62%; the SME segment is the fastest-growing at 19.56% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia Digital Transformation Market, 2025)

-
Malaysia's retail e-commerce is projected to grow from US$10.62 billion (2025) to US$23.11 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 13.67%; B2B e-commerce will be the fastest-growing segment at 15.63% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-Commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
Digital media's share of total Malaysian adex is forecast to rise to 85% by 2029, from about 77% in 2024.
(Source: MAGNA, reported by Bernama, 2026)

-
Malaysia's influencer marketing market is projected to grow from US$82.42 million (2026) to US$119.29 million by 2030 at an annual growth rate of 9.14%.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Programmatic advertising is forecast to account for 73% of Malaysia's total digital ad spend by 2028, up from under 50% today.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
5G is projected to represent 84% of all mobile subscriptions in Malaysia by 2029. MCMC counted 28.7 million 5G subscriptions in November 2025.
(Sources: GlobalData, reported by RCR Wireless, 2025; MCMC, reported by Malay Mail, 2025)

-
Malaysia's data centre infrastructure market is projected to grow from US$5.48 billion (2025) to US$16.02 billion by 2031 at a 19.55% CAGR; Johor is projected to hold 60% of national capacity by 2030.
(Source: Digital in Asia / Mordor Intelligence, 2025)

### Frequently Asked Questions

How big is Malaysia's digital marketing market in 2026?
The latest published figures cover 2024 and 2025. Digital advertising took about 77% of all Malaysian ad spend in 2024, and MAGNA forecasts that share will reach 85% by 2029. The e-Conomy SEA 2025 report (Google, Temasek, Bain) projected Malaysia's digital economy GMV at US$39 billion for 2025, up 19% year on year and the fastest growth in Southeast Asia.

Which social media platforms are most popular in Malaysia?
As of late 2025, measured by platform-reported ad reach: TikTok reports 30.7 million (86.8% of internet users), followed by YouTube at 23.6 million (66.7%), Facebook at 23.0 million (65.0%), Instagram at 16.1 million (45.5%), and LinkedIn at 10.0 million registered members (28.3%). DataReportal notes TikTok's figure exceeds the adult population, so read it as ad reach, not unique users. Source: DataReportal Digital 2026: Malaysia.

How many Malaysians use the internet?
Malaysia had approximately 35.4 million internet users as of October 2025, representing 98% of the total population (DataReportal Digital 2026). In the Digital 2025 edition, Malaysians spent an average of 8 hours 13 minutes online daily, one of the highest figures in Southeast Asia. Sources: DataReportal Digital 2025 and Digital 2026: Malaysia.

What is the e-commerce market size in Malaysia?
Malaysia's e-commerce sector GMV was projected to reach US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY, e-Conomy SEA 2025), with the retail e-commerce segment valued at US$10.62 billion. The DOSM's broader measure of e-commerce income reached RM1.29 trillion in 2024. 72.67% of e-commerce transactions are completed via smartphone. Sources: e-Conomy SEA 2025, Mordor Intelligence, DOSM.

How widely are Malaysian businesses adopting AI in marketing?
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools daily, and apps with marketed AI features saw 103% revenue growth in H1 2025 vs H1 2024. However, 73% of Malaysian businesses currently using AI remain at basic automation levels. Malaysia attracted 32% of Southeast Asia's private AI funding (US$759 million) between H2 2024 and H1 2025. Sources: e-Conomy SEA 2025, Digital in Asia.

How does Malaysia compare to other Southeast Asian countries digitally?
Malaysia's internet penetration is 98%, level with Singapore (98.4%) and just behind Brunei (99.0%), the highest in Southeast Asia (DataReportal Digital 2026). Malaysians use an average of 8.12 social platforms each month, second in SEA behind the Philippines at 8.36, and spend 8 hours 13 minutes online daily, also second only to the Philippines (DataReportal Digital 2025). Malaysia's digital economy grew 19% in 2025, the fastest in SEA (e-Conomy SEA 2025).
